items.followUp: Define a rigid body and state what is meant by the moment arm of a force.

rubric.why: This states the defining property of a rigid body.
rubric.description: A rigid body is one in which the distance between any two particles remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the distances between particles or the body's shape remain unchanged.

rubric.why: This identifies the perpendicular distance that determines the turning effect of a force.
rubric.description: The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the line of action of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the moment arm as the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the force's line of action.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is a body in which the distance between any two particles remains unchanged when forces act on it.
The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the line of action of a force.

items.followUp: Explain how altitude and latitude affect the value of g.

rubric.why: Identifies that g varies with location-dependent factors.
rubric.description: The value of g varies from place to place because it depends on factors such as altitude, latitude, and distance from Earth's centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying at least one relevant factor affecting g.

rubric.why: Explains a correct way in which g changes with location.
rubric.description: As altitude increases, g decreases; g also varies with latitude because of Earth's rotation and shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that g decreases with altitude or that latitude-related variation is due to Earth's rotation.

modelAnswer: The value of g varies from place to place because it depends on the distance from Earth's centre and on latitude.
As altitude increases, the distance from Earth's centre increases, so g decreases.
The value of g also varies with latitude because Earth rotates and is not perfectly spherical.
